records.name: Med Ball Rotational Scoop Toss
records.description: Perform Med Ball Rotational Scoop Toss with a light-to-moderate medicine ball. Load the body through the feet and hips, rotate with a stacked trunk, release or catch cleanly, and reset before the next throw.

coachingExecution.movement_description: Perform Med Ball Rotational Scoop Toss with a light-to-moderate medicine ball. Load the body through the feet and hips, rotate with a stacked trunk, release or catch cleanly, and reset before the next throw.
setup: Clear the training area and define the athlete's start position, finish position, and stop command.
Choose a medicine ball light enough to move fast without changing posture or release path.
Use a solid wall and stand far enough away that the ball rebound or release is safe.
Coach one clean practice rep before adding load, speed, partner input, or decision demand.
execution_steps: Start in the prescribed stance and create quiet tension through feet, hips, and trunk.
Load or reorient under control, then express the throw, jump, cut, or sprint with high intent.
Stick, catch, release, or finish cleanly; reset fully before the next attempt.
coach_cues: Rotate from the ground up.
Ribs and pelvis travel as a team.
Own the finish before the next rep.
Fast intent, low volume.
Throw or move through the target, not through your low back.
common_faults: Low back becomes the main rotation point.
Feet lose pressure or the athlete spins on the toes without a controlled base.
Ribs flare, shoulders shrug, or pelvis dumps forward during the turn.
Too many reps turn power into conditioning.
Throw or cut accuracy drops but the set continues anyway.
Ball is too heavy, making the throw slow or arm-dominant.
breathing_cues: Exhale through effort or release.
Do not hold breath to force rotation.
Recover breathing before the next high-intent rep.
coachingExecution.quality_gate: The attempt counts only if speed or throw intent is high, the rotation is sequenced from the ground up, the landing/finish is controlled, and the athlete can reset without rushing.
stop_signs: Sharp pain, joint pinch, numbness, tingling, dizziness, or symptom increase.
Lumbar spine becomes the main source of rotation instead of hips, pelvis, thoracic spine, and shoulders.
The athlete loses foot pressure, trunk stack, safe landing, throw accuracy, or controlled reset.
Throw speed, jump/contact quality, cut angle, or acceleration intent drops noticeably.

records.name: Cable / Band Chop
records.description: Stand, kneel, or half-kneel and move the band or cable on a diagonal chop path with deliberate control.

coachingExecution.movement_description: Stand, kneel, or half-kneel and move the band or cable on a diagonal chop path with deliberate control.
setup: Clear the floor or training lane and choose the easiest variation the athlete can control.
Stand, kneel, or half-kneel and move the band or cable on a diagonal chop path with deliberate control.
Set ribs over pelvis, establish quiet breathing, and define the stop rule before the first rep.
execution_steps: Begin Cable / Band Chop from the coached start position.
Move slowly enough that the trunk, pelvis, shoulder, and hip positions remain organized.
Breathe behind the brace instead of holding air or grinding.
Pause briefly at the hardest point, then return under control.
Stop the set when the athlete cannot repeat the same position.
coach_cues: Ribs over pelvis.
Breathe behind the brace.
Move only through the range you own.
Quiet hips, quiet ribs.
Stop before the position changes.
breathing_cues: Exhale without crunching.
Use a brace you can breathe through.
Reset if breath-holding becomes the strategy.
common_faults: Rib flare or low-back arching.
Breath-holding or neck tension.
Hip shift, pelvis rotation, or shoulder collapse.
Using speed, momentum, or fatigue to hide poor control.
quality_gate: Athlete can breathe while maintaining the target shape.
Left and right sides look similar enough for the intended level.
No pain, pinching, dizziness, or uncontrolled pressure symptoms.
Reps remain repeatable without coach constantly rescuing the position.
stop_signs: Back pain, neck symptoms, dizziness, or sharp joint pain.
Visible rib flare, lumbar sag, or pelvic shift that cannot be corrected.
Athlete cannot continue breathing behind the brace.
The drill turns into a conditioning challenge instead of control practice.

records.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
records.description: Dumbbell Floor Press is a dumbbell-loaded strength exercise for upper-body pressing force. Load, range, tempo, and rest should support force production rather than metabolic fatigue.

coachingExecution.movement_description: Dumbbell Floor Press: Horizontal pressing pattern with a floor stop that builds chest and triceps strength with shoulder range control. Use load that lets the athlete control the entire rep and finish with the same alignment they started with.
setup: Select dumbbells that can be pressed without joint compensation for Dumbbell Floor Press.
Set the shoulder blades and grip before the first rep.
Brace ribs over pelvis; avoid flaring to create false range.
Begin from a stable floor, bench, kneeling, seated, or standing setup as the variation requires.
execution_steps: Press the dumbbells through the prescribed path without shrugging or rib flare.
Control the lowering phase and keep elbows tracking naturally.
Finish each rep with joints stacked and shoulders stable.
Pause or reset when speed or line changes.
coach_cues: Own the setup before the rep.
Brace, then move the dumbbell.
Control down; drive up without losing shape.
Stop before strength turns into survival.
athlete_cues: Move the weight, not your joints.
Leave one clean rep in reserve.
breathing_cues: Inhale before the lowering or reset.
Brace through the hard portion.
Exhale without collapsing posture.
common_faults: Chasing load before position is repeatable.
Holding the breath for the entire set instead of bracing and breathing.
Rushing the eccentric or bouncing out of the bottom.
Ribs flare or shoulders shrug to finish the press.
quality_gate: Final rep looks close to the first rep.
stop_signs: Pain appears or increases during the set.
Technique changes more than one rep in a row.
Breathing becomes dizziness, bracing panic, or uncontrolled breath holding.
Grip, shoulder, spine, hip, knee, or ankle position becomes unsafe.
